about.title: Alhambra Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product does not care whether you bought it at a shop along Main Street, ordered it online to a home near Mission Road, or drove it off a lot before merging onto the I-10. When something you trusted fails — a space heater, a child's car seat, a power tool, a medication, a tire — the harm can be sudden and serious. Alhambra residents in Los Angeles County have a meaningful advantage under California law: product liability claims are often built on strict liability. That means you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. You do not have to prove the company was careless. In 2025, Alhambra recorded 301 injury collisions and 418 people hurt; when an airbag fails to deploy or a seatbelt gives way, the crash file is only part of the story. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Alhambra Residents Use LawProactive for Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In most California product cases you are not asked to prove the maker was negligent, only that the product was defective and that defect hurt you. Attorneys in our network understand how to frame a design, manufacturing, or warning defect from the start.

items.title: More than one company may be responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer that sold you the item can all share liability under California law. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim, even when parts were made overseas.

items.title: Preserving the product is step one
items.desc: The item that injured you is usually the central piece of evidence, and tossing or repairing it can undermine a claim. Connecting with an attorney early helps ensure the product, packaging, and receipts are kept intact.

items.question: The product that hurt me was destroyed or badly damaged. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. Keep whatever remains, including fragments, packaging, manuals, and receipts, and photograph everything before moving it. An attorney can often rely on the remaining pieces, purchase records, and similar units of the same model to establish a defect. The important thing is to stop anyone from discarding or repairing the item now.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Valley Boulevard, but I think a vehicle part failed. Is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be both. A collision claim against another driver and a product claim against the maker of a defective airbag, brake, or tire are separate paths, and they can proceed together. Alhambra police reports document the crash itself, but proving the part failed usually requires preserving the vehicle and having it inspected before it is salvaged. An attorney can help place a hold on the car through your insurer.

items.question: Do I need to show the company knew about the defect?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability approach focuses on whether the product was defective in its design, manufacture, or warnings and whether that defect caused your injury. What the company knew can matter for other issues, but it is not something you must prove just to bring the claim. An independent attorney can explain which theory best fits your situation.
